pr_title: Add more iaqualink entity properties, fix timeout issues
pr_body:
## Description:

* Update iaqualink-py to 0.3.0.
* Implement assumed_state, available and device_info.
* Remove the aiohttp timeout that was a workaround for bad locking logic in iaqualink-py.
* Use async_get_clientsession instead of async_create_clientsession.

**Related issue (if applicable):** fixes #27642 

**Pull request with documentation for [home-assistant.io](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io) (if applicable):** home-assistant/home-assistant.io#<home-assistant.io PR number goes here>

  - [x] Local tests pass with `tox`. **Your PR cannot be merged unless tests pass**
  - [x] There is no commented out code in this PR.
  - [x] I have followed the [development checklist][dev-checklist]

If user exposed functionality or configuration variables are added/changed:
  - [x] Documentation added/updated in [home-assistant.io](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io)

If the code communicates with devices, web services, or third-party tools:
  - [x] [_The manifest file_][manifest-docs] has all fields filled out correctly. Update and include derived files by running `python3 -m script.hassfest`.
  - [x] New or updated dependencies have been added to `requirements_all.txt` by running `python3 -m script.gen_requirements_all`.

If the code does not interact with devices:

issue_context.title: 100.2 - Aqualink timeout issue
issue_context.body:
After upgrading to 100.2 the aqualink integration seems to not load randomly after restarts... 

Sometimes it takes 2-3 restarts for it to load properly or a removal and re-add of the integration.
```
Mon Oct 14 2019 09:05:46 GMT-0400 (Eastern Daylight Time)
Error setting up entry XXXX for iaqualink
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/srv/homeassistant/lib/python3.7/site-packages/homeassistant/config_entries.py", line 190, in async_setup
    hass, self
  File "/srv/homeassistant/lib/python3.7/site-packages/homeassistant/components/iaqualink/__init__.py", line 91, in async_setup_entry
    await aqualink.login()
  File "/srv/homeassistant/lib/python3.7/site-packages/iaqualink/client.py", line 102, in login
    r = await self._send_login_request()
  File "/srv/homeassistant/lib/python3.7/site-packages/iaqualink/client.py", line 99, in _send_login_request
    return await self._send_request(AQUALINK_LOGIN_URL, method="post", json=data)
  File "/srv/homeassistant/lib/python3.7/site-packages/iaqualink/client.py", line 85, in _send_request
    method, url, headers=AQUALINK_HTTP_HEADERS, **kwargs
  File "/srv/homeassistant/lib/python3.7/site-packages/aiohttp/client.py", line 504, in _request
    await resp.start(conn)
  File "/srv/homeassistant/lib/python3.7/site-packages/aiohttp/client_reqrep.py", line 860, in start
    self._continue = None
  File "/srv/homeassistant/lib/python3.7/site-packages/aiohttp/helpers.py", line 586, in __exit__
    raise asyncio.TimeoutError from None
concurrent.futures._base.TimeoutError
```

Bumped the timeout to 30 seconds and all works fine.
comments: Hey there @flz, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`iaqualink`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L142) for? Thanks!
I'll try to figure out what the best practices are setting timeouts but I'm surprised that the request doesn't complete within 5 seconds. What's your latency to iaqualink-api.realtime.io (use ping)?

I have a similar latency at home. Not sure why the login times out for you.

I introduced the 5s timeout in 0.100.2 (default was 5m before). The high timeout caused the UI to become unresponsive when requests would occasionally hang. I've since removed some non-async-safe locking from the API which may have caused the hang. I'll do some extra testing to see if we can get away with returning to the previous timeout (or bump it to 30s, which is still high but better than 5m).
Apologies for the delay. I've had this patch in testing for a while to make sure there were no regressions due to removing the timeout.

Thanks, @flz when do you see the update being applied?  I don't mind trying it out as well.

Thanks!

The changes have landed in the dev branch which means it will be in the next release of homeassistant (0.102.0). According to the schedule, it should be released on 11/20.

review_comments: Will there only be one entity per device?
I'm not sure I understand the question. Do you have an example where it's not the case?
We're using the entity unique_id as identifier. If there would be more than one entity per device the mapping wouldn't be correct. This id should be unique per device and not unique per entity.
Was looking for examples where you'd have more than one entity for a given device.
I think we're good here in any case. There's a 1:1 mapping between entities and devices/controls on the iaqualink side.
